title: Adaptive genetic algorithm based deep feature selector for cancer detection in lung histopathological images
study_claim: The paper presents a genetic feature selector for classifying lung tissue images.
observation: The notebook selects features using the combined training and test labels, then splits the data again.
consequence: Estimating diagnostic accuracy on new images requires repeating feature selection inside each training split.

title: A Symmetric Maximum-Entropy Characterisation of the Weibull Distribution via Fractional Moments.
study_claim: A specific Weibull distribution maximizes entropy under a second-moment constraint.
observation: The condition E[X²]=1 does not make Weibull(2,1) a maximum-entropy distribution.
consequence: The constraint alone cannot identify that Weibull distribution as the unique solution.

title: A novel extension of the exponential distribution with application in modeling complex lifetime and environmental data.
study_claim: The paper derives the variance of an extended exponential distribution.
observation: The published formula can return a negative variance.
consequence: The formula cannot measure dispersion across the full stated parameter range.

title: Application of Ujlayan-Dixit Fractional Exponential Probability Distribution.
study_claim: The fractional exponential model defines cumulative probabilities for the stated parameters.
observation: The proposed cumulative probability can exceed one.
consequence: For those parameters the formula fails to yield valid probabilities.

title: Applications of Ujlayan and Dixit Fractional Uniform Probability Distribution.
study_claim: The paper gives a cumulative distribution for a fractional extension of the uniform distribution.
observation: Fα(x)=exp(((1−α)/α)(b−x))(x−a)/(b−a) can exceed one.
consequence: The extension loses its probability interpretation for some permitted parameters.

title: Application of Ujlayan-Dixit Fractional Chi-Square Probability Distribution.
study_claim: The proposed function generalizes the chi-square distribution over the specified domain.
observation: The stated domain permits negative densities.
consequence: Using this extension to model data requires restricting its parameters.

title: Application of Ujlayan-Dixit (UD) Fractional Gamma With Two-Parameters Probability Distribution.
study_claim: The formula defines a two-parameter fractional gamma distribution.
observation: The stated domain permits negative densities.
consequence: The proposed family needs a restricted domain before it can estimate probabilities.

title: Optimising hyperparameters with a tree structured Parzen estimator to improve diabetes prediction
study_claim: Hyperparameter tuning improves the classifier's ability to detect diabetes.
observation: The authors used the test set to tune 50 configurations and reported performance on that same set.
consequence: Confirming diabetes-detection accuracy requires patients excluded from tuning.

title: A hybrid compound scaling hypergraph neural network for robust cervical cancer subtype classification using whole slide cytology images
study_claim: The network achieves 100% F1 for the superficial-intermediate cervical subtype.
observation: The stated F1 exceeds the bounds implied by the reported precision and recall.
consequence: Those two metrics rule out a perfect F1 score for that subtype.

title: FedMedSecure: federated few-shot learning with cross-attention mechanisms and explainable AI for collaborative healthcare cybersecurity
study_claim: Grouping traffic classes reduces entropy by 68%.
observation: A benign traffic share of 73.2%, a separate BENIGN class and the reported 68% reduction cannot all hold.
consequence: Obtaining a 68% reduction would require another traffic composition or definition.

title: Distributional properties of the entropy transformed Weibull distribution and applications to various scientific fields.
study_claim: A series evaluates the characteristic function of a transformed Weibull distribution.
observation: The published series can diverge.
consequence: It cannot evaluate the characteristic function for certain parameters.

title: Optimized ANN–RF hybrid model with optuna for fault detection and classification in power transmission systems
study_claim: The electrical fault classifier achieves an F1 score of 99.6 in the main comparison.
observation: The central row gives precision 99.5, recall 99.4 and F1 99.6. Their definitions rule out this combination.
consequence: Assessing the claimed advantage requires recalculating that F1 score.

title: AttGRU-HMSI: enhancing heart disease diagnosis using hybrid deep learning approach
study_claim: The network predicts heart disease with the performance reported for the described dataset.
observation: The paper gives three incompatible descriptions of the data used.
consequence: The evaluation population for the reported diagnostic accuracy remains unclear.

title: Exploring brain-gut interaction mechanisms in Transcutaneous auricular Vagus Nerve stimulation for Major Depressive Disorder
study_claim: The study reports a statistically significant contrast in its analysis of vagal stimulation.
observation: The reported t statistic does not support the stated significance.
consequence: The evidence for this particular stimulation effect would change.

title: Altered cytokine profiles and elevated lactate levels in children with autism spectrum disorder: indications of a dysregulated immune-metabolic network?
study_claim: The study reports p=0.42 for an IQ comparison.
observation: The IQ statistic and the published p-value do not agree.
consequence: Assessing whether the groups had comparable IQ requires resolving this discrepancy.

title: Rethinking childhood-onset schizophrenia: neurodevelopmental comorbidities shape the psychopathological profile
study_claim: The study reports group differences after adjusting for IQ.
observation: The published IQ-adjusted p-values correspond to different degrees of freedom.
consequence: With the reported degrees of freedom, those adjusted differences lose statistical support.

title: A longitudinal study on the relationships between impulsivity and excessive smartphone use among patients with acquired brain injury and control participants
study_claim: The study evaluates changes in non-planning impulsivity over time.
observation: The table pairs a significant F statistic with a non-significant p-value.
consequence: The two entries support opposite conclusions about the change in impulsivity.

title: Differential effects of a single dose of Lisdexamfetamine and Guanfacine on cognitive function in children with ADHD
study_claim: Test order significantly affects the pharmacological analysis.
observation: The reported F statistic does not support the stated order effect.
consequence: This comparison provides insufficient evidence for an order effect.

title: Hierarchical Hybrid Sliced Wasserstein: A Scalable Metric for Heterogeneous Joint Distributions
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (NeurIPS 2024), Main Conference Track
study_claim: Marginal distances can bound the distance between the joint distributions considered.
observation: Proposition 3(i,ii) uses marginal distances to bound a joint distance without requiring independence.
consequence: With dependent variables, the marginals can miss differences in their joint distribution.

title: OFC-induced network modularity improves positive symptoms and attentional alertness in schizophrenia: a combined rTMS-fMRI study
study_claim: The stated correction identifies significant changes in brain networks.
observation: The reported adjusted probabilities disagree with the source data and the stated correction.
consequence: Applying the stated multiple-comparison correction changes which associations cross the significance threshold.

title: Hierarchical Sliced Wasserstein Distance
study_claim: The hierarchical distance achieves the stated sample rate for any transport order.
observation: Proposition 4 gives O(sqrt(log(n)/n)) for every p≥1 without additional regularity assumptions.
consequence: For higher transport orders, that accuracy guarantee requires additional assumptions.

title: Energy-Based Sliced Wasserstein Distance
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (NeurIPS 2023), Main Conference Track
study_claim: The energy-weighted projection distance characterizes weak convergence.
observation: Theorem 2 claims equivalence with weak convergence without controlling moments.
consequence: Weak convergence alone cannot determine how the proposed distance behaves.

title: Revisiting Sliced Wasserstein on Images: From Vectorization to Convolution
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS 2022), Main Conference Track
study_claim: The image estimator achieves the stated rate at any transport order.
observation: Proposition 3 gives O(sqrt(log(n)/n)) for every p≥1.
consequence: Achieving a target accuracy may require more images than the rate suggests.

title: KFNN: K-Free Nearest Neighbor For Crowdsourcing
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (NeurIPS 2024), Main Conference Track
study_claim: The learned distance brings members of the same class closer together.
observation: Corollary 2 claims that same-class distances are smaller than Euclidean distances.
consequence: The model can move same-class neighbors farther apart despite the proposed guarantee.

title: Plasma proteomics identify biomarkers predicting Parkinson’s disease up to 7 years before symptom onset
study_claim: A particular panel of plasma proteins predicts Parkinson's disease.
observation: Mapping support_ to protein names drops two extra columns, shifting the selected protein identities.
consequence: The reported Parkinson's panel may differ from the proteins the mathematical procedure selected.

title: Metabolomic machine learning predictor for diagnosis and prognosis of gastric cancer
study_claim: A metabolic signature predicts gastric cancer in patients held out for internal validation.
observation: LASSO selection uses splits of 426 participants. The 142 patients in the internal test come from those same 426.
consequence: Internal classification accuracy needs a cohort independent of feature selection.

title: Functional protein mining with conformal guarantees
study_claim: The procedure selects functional candidates subject to a statistical risk guarantee.
observation: When no threshold passes certification, np.argmax(all_false) returns 0 and selects the lowest threshold.
consequence: The algorithm can accept protein candidates even when no threshold certifies the risk.

title: A deep learning system for predicting time to progression of diabetic retinopathy
study_claim: The model uses observed intervals to estimate time to retinopathy progression.
observation: The interval likelihood uses S(t)F(t′). The interval probability is F(t′)−F(t).
consequence: The model learns from probabilities that differ from those of the observed intervals.

title: A gut microbial signature for combination immune checkpoint blockade across cancer types
study_claim: A microbial signature predicts immunotherapy response in held-out evaluation groups.
observation: Hyperparameter tuning uses all 77 patients, including patients later placed in the evaluation groups.
consequence: Performance on new patients needs an independent evaluation.

title: Markovian Sliced Wasserstein Distances: Beyond Independent Projections
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (NeurIPS 2023), Main Conference Track
study_claim: Markovian projections achieve the stated sample rate and characterize weak convergence.
observation: Proposition 2 claims O(sqrt(log(n)/n)) for all p≥1. Theorem 2 equates weak convergence with convergence in MSW.
consequence: Without moment control, the stated sample-size and distance-convergence guarantees can fail.

title: Sliced Wasserstein with Random-Path Projecting Directions
journal: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR235:37879–37899
study_claim: Random projections attain the stated sample rate on compactly supported distributions.
observation: Proposition 2 claims O(sqrt(log(n+1)/n)) for p>1 on compact support.
consequence: Sampling error can decrease more slowly even on compact support.

title: Neural Projection Fusion for Sliced Wasserstein on the Hypersphere
journal: Proceedings of the Thirty-Fifth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Main Track:5306–5314
study_claim: Conditions on spherical moments allow the projected distributions to be compared.
observation: The spherical moments controlled in Proposition 2 do not control the stereographic projection.
consequence: Those conditions alone cannot guarantee a finite projected distance.

title: Fast and interpretable quantification of biological shape heterogeneity via stratified Wasserstein kernel
study_claim: The representation distinguishes shapes up to distance-preserving transformations.
observation: Theorem 2 asserts injectivity up to isometry under H1. Two continuous shapes satisfy H1 yet share an embedding.
consequence: The same descriptor can represent distinct biological shapes even after accounting for isometries.

title: Noninvasive proteomic biomarkers for alcohol-related liver disease
study_claim: Cross-validation measures the diagnostic performance of liver disease biomarkers.
observation: Supervised mRMR selection uses the entire cohort before cross-validation reuses those patients.
consequence: Internal biomarker validation needs to be repeated with independent feature selection.

title: Machine learning-based integration develops an immune-derived lncRNA signature for improving outcomes in colorectal cancer
study_claim: Concordance in external cohorts measures the trained signature's prognostic value.
observation: The C-index uses a Cox model fitted to external outcomes. This can reverse the original predictor's risk ranking.
consequence: The reported external concordance can reward the opposite of the trained risk ranking.

title: Non-Exchangeable Conformal Risk Control
study_claim: The threshold defined by the infimum controls risk under the theorem's conditions.
observation: Theorem 1 requires bounded, monotone losses. Feasibility of the infimum also needs right continuity here.
consequence: The selected threshold can exceed the allowed risk even when feasible candidates satisfy it.

title: Post-encoding administration of oxytocin selectively enhances memory consolidation of male faces in females
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
study_claim: Oxytocin improves recall of male faces among women in the simple contrast.
observation: For that contrast, the reported p=.05 disagrees with the t statistic and source data.
consequence: The simple male-face contrast loses significance. The interaction by face type persists.

title: Distance-Based Tree-Sliced Wasserstein Distance
study_claim: The distance is invariant to Euclidean transformations for the allowed samplers.
observation: Theorem 5.2 fixes an arbitrary sampler, but the proof changes its distribution.
consequence: Rotating the same data can change the distance computed with a fixed sampler.

title: Tree-Sliced Entropy Partial Transport
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems38, Main Conference Track
study_claim: Partial tree transport is invariant under rigid transformations.
observation: The fixed tree distribution in Theorem 3.3 lacks the required Euclidean symmetry.
consequence: Rigidly transforming both datasets can change their tree-based distance.

title: Tree-Sliced Wasserstein Distance with Nonlinear Projection
journal: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR267:60001–60033
study_claim: The construction defines a metric for every allowed continuous injective transformation.
observation: Theorem 5.3 claims SpatialTSW is a metric for every such transformation. Some destroy integrability.
consequence: An allowed projection can give an infinite distance even for admissible inputs.

title: Tree-Sliced Wasserstein Distance: A Geometric Perspective
journal: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR267:59969–60000
study_claim: The tree distance distinguishes all distributions under the allowed samplers.
observation: Theorem 5.2 claims the identity property without requiring enough informative directions.
consequence: Distinct distributions can have distance zero when the sampler misses informative directions.

title: Tree-sliced Sobolev IPM
study_claim: A subtree-length penalty regularizes the proposed distance.
observation: The model uses complete lines whose subtrees can have infinite length.
consequence: The proposed penalty can be infinite on the model's own space.

title: Distinguishing features of long COVID identified through immune profiling
study_claim: Validation RMSE summarizes the accuracy of the logistic predictions.
observation: Validation compares binary labels directly to logits when computing RMSE.
consequence: The reported error does not measure the discrepancy between predicted probabilities and observed diagnoses.

title: Spatial cellular architecture predicts prognosis in glioblastoma
study_claim: The model uses the specified spatial normalization to represent interactions between cells.
observation: The code normalizes interactions differently from Equation 5.
consequence: Cell interactions estimated by the code do not reproduce the described prognostic model.

title: Sliced-Wasserstein on Symmetric Positive Definite Matrices for M/EEG Signals
study_claim: The distance on positive-definite matrices characterizes weak convergence.
observation: Theorem 2.7 equates weak convergence with convergence in SPDSW without requiring moment convergence.
consequence: Sequences can converge weakly without approaching each other in the proposed distance.

title: Efficient Sliced Wasserstein Distance Computation via Adaptive Bayesian Optimization
study_claim: The proposed angular function gives a Gaussian-process covariance for optimization.
observation: The angular RBF covariance produces indefinite Gram matrices for allowed inputs.
consequence: The Bayesian optimizer can receive an invalid covariance for those directions.

title: Sliced-Wasserstein Distances and Flows on Cartan-Hadamard Manifolds
study_claim: The distance on Cartan–Hadamard manifolds characterizes weak convergence.
observation: Proposition 27 equates weak convergence with convergence in CHSW without requiring moment convergence.
consequence: Equivalence of these convergence notions requires control of the distribution tails.

title: Mixed-Curvature Tree-Sliced Wasserstein Distance
study_claim: The proposed tree-based distance is a metric for the distributions considered.
observation: The metric claim allows any probability law over trees without a sufficient support condition.
consequence: Distinct distributions can be indistinguishable under an allowed tree law.

title: A multimodal sleep foundation model for disease prediction
study_claim: The survival objective learns disease risks from sleep records.
observation: cox_ph_loss depends on arbitrary row order when event and censoring times coincide.
consequence: Prognostic training can depend on the administrative ordering of ties.

title: Augmented Sliced Wasserstein Distances
study_claim: The augmented projection gives a valid distance for distributions with finite moments.
observation: Injectivity of g does not ensure finite moments after transformation.
consequence: The augmented distance can be infinite even when the original distributions have finite moments.

title: Customized Gaussian process for representing polycrystalline texture
journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 440:117934
study_claim: A function of geodesic distance models covariance in crystal textures.
observation: The squared-exponential geodesic kernel is indefinite on permitted spherical configurations.
consequence: The proposed crystal-texture covariance can fail to define a Gaussian process.

title: Stochastic inference of effective material properties from crystallographic textures via Gaussian process regression
journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 453:118825
study_claim: The proposed geodesic covariance quantifies uncertainty in material properties.
observation: The geodesic Matérn covariance produces indefinite matrices and negative predictive variances.
consequence: The materials model can return invalid predictive uncertainties.

title: Deep Random Features for Scalable Interpolation of Spatiotemporal Data
study_claim: The model's random features approximate the specified spherical covariance.
observation: The released spherical features approximate a different spectrum from that of the stated Matérn covariance.
consequence: The program's spherical interpolation approximates a different covariance.

title: Assessment of global health risk of antibiotic resistance genes
study_claim: Validation estimates how well the classifier identifies antibiotic resistance risks.
observation: RandomForest is trained on every record before the validation loop. The training folds are never used.
consequence: The reported performance cannot establish accuracy on previously unseen resistance records.

title: Ensemble Forecasts of Solar Wind Connectivity to 1 Rs Using ADAPT-WSA
study_claim: The forecast region contains the stated probability for solar-wind connectivity.
observation: The integral of a spherical density omits the area factor cos(latitude).
consequence: Forecast coverage can vary artificially with latitude.

title: Scalable Sobolev IPM for Probability Measures on a Graph
journal: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:32771–32802
study_claim: A closed-form expression evaluates the proposed Sobolev distance on graphs.
observation: The closed form allows atomic measures incompatible with the required continuity of the critic.
consequence: For atomic measures on graphs, the fast formula can disagree with the defined distance.

title: Sobolev Transport: A Scalable Metric for Probability Measures with Graph Metrics
journal: Proceedings of The 25th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics, PMLR 151:9844–9868
study_claim: A graph transport formula equals optimization over the permitted functions.
observation: The formula integrates atomic derivatives incompatible with the required continuity of the critic.
consequence: For point masses, the Sobolev transport calculation can solve a different problem.

title: Scalable Unbalanced Sobolev Transport for Measures on a Graph
journal: Proceedings of The 26th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics, PMLR 206:8521–8560
study_claim: An explicit formula computes Sobolev transport between measures of unequal mass.
observation: The formula integrates atomic derivatives incompatible with the required continuity of the critic.
consequence: The closed-form unbalanced transport value can violate the original graph constraints.

title: Generalized Sobolev Transport for Probability Measures on a Graph
journal: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235:26152–26174
study_claim: Generalized Sobolev transport admits a closed form on the graph.
observation: The formula integrates atomic derivatives incompatible with the required continuity of the critic.
consequence: The generalized transport cost can be inconsistent with the permitted class of functions.

title: An Efficient Orlicz-Sobolev Approach for Transporting Unbalanced Measures on a Graph
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38
study_claim: The proposed formula efficiently computes unbalanced Orlicz–Sobolev transport.
observation: The formula integrates atomic derivatives incompatible with the required continuity of the critic.
consequence: The formula can assign a cost that no permitted continuous critic can achieve.

title: Riemannian Optimization on Relaxed Indicator Matrix Manifold
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: The graph-partitioning objective has a uniformly bounded gradient.
observation: Theorem 6 bounds the Ratio Cut gradient uniformly. The gradient is unbounded on the stated domain.
consequence: This bound cannot guarantee uniform stability when optimizing the graph partition.

title: Biomarker panels for improved risk prediction and enhanced biological insights in patients with atrial fibrillation
study_claim: The biomarker panels distinguish risk groups with the reported AUCs.
observation: LASSO evaluates the patients used for fitting. Cross-validation selects lambda but does not supply the reported predictions. XGBoost also evaluates its training matrix.
consequence: These AUCs measure fit to known patients. External prognostic accuracy remains open.

title: Learning Molecular Chirality via Chiral Determinant Kernels
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: The proposed determinant consistently encodes molecular orientation under rotation.
observation: Lemma 4.1 uses the determinant of R in a rectangular QR decomposition. The code returns opposite signs for rigidly rotated configurations.
consequence: A rigid rotation can change the sign used to distinguish molecular chirality.

title: Selective Generation for Controllable Language Models
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems37, NeurIPS2024, Spotlight
study_claim: The procedure chooses a certified threshold to control generation risk.
observation: Calibration can return a threshold even when none passes certification. The next step assumes a valid certificate.
consequence: The generator can produce text without the claimed risk guarantee.

title: Revisiting Nonstationary Kernel Design for Multi-Output Gaussian Processes
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: The specified Hermitian symmetry suffices for constructing multi-output covariances.
observation: Theorem 2 requires Hermitian symmetry but omits joint positivity across outputs.
consequence: The proposed symmetry permits invalid Gaussian-process covariances.

title: Multi-View Oriented GPLVM: Expressiveness and Efficiency
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025), Main Conference Track
study_claim: The Gaussian mixture family can approximate any continuous kernel arbitrarily well.
observation: All NG-SM mixtures force variance to be maximal at the origin.
consequence: The mixtures cannot approximate kernels whose variance increases away from the origin.

title: Epigenomic diagnosis and prognosis of Acute Myeloid Leukemia
study_claim: The epigenomic classifier predicts five-year survival in acute myeloid leukemia.
observation: It treats early-censored patients as known five-year survivors: 373 of 946 training patients and 23 patients in the binary AML02/08 evaluation.
consequence: The five-year estimates depend on outcomes that were still unknown.

title: Hybrid vision GNNs based early detection and protection against pest diseases in coffee plants
study_claim: The model classifies coffee diseases with the performance summarized in the table.
observation: The confusion counts do not agree with the reported precision, recall, F1 and accuracy.
consequence: The published counts leave the actual classification performance unresolved.

title: An Efficient SE(p)-Invariant Transport Metric Driven by Polar Transport Discrepancy-based Representation
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: Optimization over reference distributions defines a finite distance.
observation: Equation (7) maximizes over references of unbounded scale. The supremum is infinite even between two centered two-point distributions.
consequence: The proposed distance can be infinite for elementary discrete distributions.

title: Meta-encoder: a unified integration framework for multiple pathological foundation models in cancer detection
study_claim: Cross-attention integrates three encoders' representations for cancer detection.
observation: With a sequence of length one, softmax returns one. The branch discards the two query encoders and depends only on the value encoder.
consequence: The attention branch can supply information from just one of the three encoders.

title: SAFER: Risk-Constrained Sample-then-Filter in Large Language Models
study_claim: Stage two filters responses using the selected evaluation criterion.
observation: StageII uses semantic similarity even when ROUGE, entailment or LLM evaluation is requested.
consequence: The filtering results support conclusions about semantic similarity only.

title: TransformEHR: transformer-based encoder-decoder generative model to enhance prediction of disease outcomes using electronic health records
study_claim: The reported AUROC summarizes discrimination across clinical predictions.
observation: The code averages AUROCs from individual minibatches, omitting comparisons between batches.
consequence: Regrouping identical predictions can change the reported ability to distinguish patients.

title: A Spectral-Grassmann Wasserstein metric for operator representations of dynamical systems
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: The spectral representation of a dynamical system determines a unique subspace.
observation: Eigenvalue multiplicities permitted by Theorem 1 break uniqueness. Mixing a basis changes the subspace of individual projectors.
consequence: The distance between systems can depend on the basis for the same eigenspace.

title: Elastic Optimal Transport: Theory, Application, and Empirical Evaluation
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: The numerical solver optimizes the stated strictly convex entropic extension.
observation: The published functional is concave. The official solver solves a different problem.
consequence: The numerical solution cannot establish uniqueness for the published objective.

title: Skin cancer detection using dermoscopic images with convolutional neural network
study_claim: The reported metrics compare networks for skin cancer classification.
observation: Figure 12's confusion matrices do not reproduce the metrics in Tables 9–10 and 14.
consequence: Comparing the networks requires reconciling the tables and matrices.

title: Learning the natural history of human disease with generative transformers
study_claim: The mask excludes information about simultaneous events when forecasting clinical outcomes.
observation: mask_ties removes simultaneous keys and values but retains their embeddings through residual connections and queries.
consequence: The model can still access simultaneous information when forecasting clinical events.

title: A foundation model for generalizable cancer diagnosis and survival prediction from histopathological images
study_claim: The prognostic model is evaluated on patients separate from model selection.
observation: The public splits reuse the entire validation set as the test set. Validation loss selects the stopping epoch. These splits reproduce 25 published C-indices.
consequence: The reproduced concordance measures performance on patients used to select the model.

title: GraftIQ: Hybrid multi-class neural network integrating clinical insight for multi-outcome prediction in liver transplant recipients
study_claim: Adding clinical variables improves post-transplant outcome prediction.
observation: Clinical_Insight.py loses test-set identities and selects the first n clinical rows.
consequence: Assessing the benefit of clinical information requires matching each prediction to its patient.

title: Multi-modal learning with incomplete data
study_claim: The study evaluates multimodal learning under different missing-data mechanisms.
observation: The default MNAR and MEM branches ignore observed and hidden values. Both generate MCAR missingness with dependent indicators.
consequence: The experiments leave robustness to the specified MNAR and MEM mechanisms unmeasured.

title: Learning Survival Distributions with Individually Calibrated Asymmetric Laplace Distribution
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: Averaging quantiles recovers the quantiles of a combined survival distribution.
observation: Equation (29) equates mixture quantiles with the average component quantiles. This identity is false. The official code applies it.
consequence: The computed survival times at a given quantile can differ from the mixture's times.

title: Histopathology images predict multi-omics aberrations and prognoses in colorectal cancer patients
study_claim: Training accumulates 32 gradients and weights the classes to predict tumor alterations.
observation: Zeroing gradients for each sample prevents accumulation over 32 samples. Mean cross-entropy with batch size one cancels inverse class weights.
consequence: The reported improvements cannot be attributed to the described accumulation and class weighting.

title: Exponential-Wrapped Mechanisms: Differential Privacy on Hadamard Manifolds Made Practical
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: The error of the privacy mechanism satisfies the published geometric bound.
observation: Theorem 3.1, Equation (5), gives a bound independent of the footpoint. Its distance can amplify transverse noise arbitrarily.
consequence: The accuracy guarantee also depends on the starting position on the manifold.

title: DunedinPACNI estimates the longitudinal Pace of Aging from a single brain image to track health and disease
study_claim: The brain marker is associated with time to first dementia diagnosis.
observation: An always-true condition overwrites first-diagnosis dates with last-visit dates. Subsequent Cox regressions use those dates.
consequence: Using the first diagnosis as the event date may change the association.

title: A Bayesian Nonparametric Framework for Private, Fair, and Balanced Tabular Data Synthesis
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: The procedure protects privacy while generating tabular data with dependencies between variables.
observation: Section 4.3 carries Rhat, estimated from the original data, into Hpert. Perturbing marginals does not privatize this joint statistic.
consequence: The privacy claim needs to account for information retained in that statistic.

title: Policy Newton Algorithm in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: Newton's algorithm uses the cubic penalty derived for the given function space.
observation: Theorem 3.3 replaces the cubed RKHS norm with the cubed Euclidean coefficient norm. The general expression is (αᵀKα)^(3/2).
consequence: The Newton penalty can mismeasure the size of a step.

title: Generalizable AI predicts immunotherapy outcomes across cancers and treatments
study_claim: The method compares fine-tuning strategies with selected network components frozen.
observation: FineTuner keeps all parameters trainable in LFT and PFT. Lowering the learning rate leaves the encoder or projector trainable.
consequence: The comparison cannot isolate the effect of freezing those components.

title: SIDISH integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomics to identify high-risk cells and guide precision therapeutics through in silico perturbation
study_claim: The study tests whether a prognostic signature separates external patients by risk.
observation: It refits Cox coefficients using the evaluated cohort's outcomes, groups the same patients and applies a log-rank test that ignores this selection.
consequence: Risk separation needs testing in patients excluded from coefficient fitting.
response_status: Limitation acknowledged and referred to editor

title: Bures-Wasserstein Flow Matching for Graph Generation
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: The published velocity follows from the proposed time-dependent geometric transformation.
observation: Proposition 3, Equation (12), omits the tangent transformation's time dependence and conflicts with the derivative of Equation (11).
consequence: The trajectory's velocity can differ from the published expression.

title: Autosurv: interpretable deep learning framework for cancer survival analysis incorporating clinical and multi-omics data
study_claim: The study evaluates the final survival model independently of training choices.
observation: Test-set C-index selects checkpoints and supplies the final reported C-index. The code ignores the epoch selected during tuning.
consequence: Checkpoint selection can favor the reported test result.

title: Strongly Convex Sets in Riemannian Manifolds
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: The geometric oracle can find the optimum within the proposed subspace.
observation: Proposition F.6 restricts the oracle to span{log_X(X0),G}. The required angular symmetry fails on SPD matrices with the affine-invariant metric.
consequence: Restricting the search can miss the optimum on positive-definite matrices.

title: An agentic framework for autonomous scientific discovery in cancer pathology
study_claim: Multiple-testing correction identifies relevant associations in cancer pathology.
observation: The BH procedure uses m=int(n_tests/6) while retaining all ranks from 1 to n_tests, cutting adjusted values roughly sixfold.
consequence: Associations can cross the threshold but lose significance when all tests are counted.

title: PathExpSurv: pathway expansion for explainable survival analysis and disease gene discovery
study_claim: The survival model ranks risk using recorded follow-up times.
observation: The public Cox and C-index functions substitute row positions for times. The driver does not sort the original LGG data or its ten folds chronologically.
consequence: Glioma concordance can depend on row order within each split.

title: Riemannian Zeroth-Order Gradient Estimation with Structure-Preserving Metrics for Geodesically Incomplete Manifolds
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: The algorithm samples directions from the required uniform distribution on an ellipsoid.
observation: Algorithm 1 equates Riemannian uniformity with Euclidean surface uniformity. These measures differ when A is not scalar.
consequence: Directions along certain axes can be overrepresented, changing the gradient estimator.

title: Artificial-intelligence-based molecular classification of diffuse gliomas using rapid, label-free optical imaging
study_claim: The classifier uses fixed, pretrained genomic representations.
observation: Tran_Classifier loads and freezes the pretrained matrix, but label_lt.apply(weights_init) randomly overwrites every embedding, including frozen ones.
consequence: The classifier's advantage cannot be attributed to the contents of that pretrained matrix.

title: Scalable Random Wavelet Features: Efficient Non-Stationary Kernel Approximation with Convergence Guarantees
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: The published bound controls variability in random wavelet features.
observation: The paper bounds feature products using B² where their second moment requires B⁴. L2 normalization permits arbitrarily large amplitudes.
consequence: Uncertainty can grow faster with amplitude than the bound predicts.

title: WFR-FM: Simulation-Free Dynamic Unbalanced Optimal Transport
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026 (ICLR 2026), Main Conference
study_claim: The theorem reconstructs trajectories from the optimal transport plan.
observation: Theorem 3.1 divides the OET plan by marginal masses that can be zero. Regions without transport require additional birth and death components.
consequence: The plan alone cannot describe appearances and disappearances where no mass is transported.

title: Cox-Sage: enhancing Cox proportional hazards model with interpretable graph neural networks for cancer prognosis
study_claim: The survival model's concordance is evaluated separately from training.
observation: Test C-index controls stopping and checkpoint selection. The same test identifies the best fold.
consequence: Choosing the epoch and fold this way can favor the reported concordance.

title: A deep learning algorithm to predict risk of pancreatic cancer from disease trajectories
study_claim: The model represents which intervals remain observable before follow-up ends.
observation: get_label rounds censoring up to the next endpoint. y_mask and get_probs_golds include this unobserved endpoint as event-free.
consequence: Intervals a patient never completed can count as free of events.

title: Plasma proteomic profiles predict individual future health risk
study_claim: Transfer learning trains the predictor while keeping specified layers frozen.
observation: ResNet.py compiles before setting trainable=False. During fitting, Keras 2.7 restores the trainable states captured at compilation. No recompilation follows.
consequence: The reported performance may come from a network with more trainable layers.

title: Optimization Over a Probability Simplex
study_claim: There is a step size satisfying the published convergence conditions.
observation: Equation 15 requires Cγ≤1/2, but its definition gives Cγ>1/2 for every γ∈(0,1), contradicting footnote 2.
consequence: No step satisfies both conditions, leaving the convergence argument without this guarantee.

title: Equivariant Manifold Neural ODEs and Differential Invariants
study_claim: The models can represent the stated transformations on manifolds without extra restrictions.
observation: Theorem 15 and Corollary 16 overlook a topological obstruction involving the tangent bundle, inherited by Theorem 19 and Corollary 20. Theorem 10 has a separate false equivalence.
consequence: The topology of the space restricts which transformations the results can represent.

title: DeepKEGG: a multi-omics data integration framework with biological insights for cancer recurrence prediction and biomarker discovery
study_claim: Feature contributions explain the trained clinical model's predictions.
observation: The attribution helper opens new sessions and reinitializes variables without restoring trained weights. It also subtracts the feature count despite a stated zero baseline.
consequence: Highlighted variables can reflect random weights, undermining their clinical interpretation.

title: Artificial intelligence based multispecialty mortality prediction models for septic shock in a multicenter retrospective study
study_claim: The model can issue an early alert during an intensive-care stay.
observation: It requires final ICU length of stay, information available only at discharge. Retrospective validation does not establish early use.
consequence: Prospective performance needs evaluation using only information available on the prediction day.

title: In-hospital mortality, readmission, and prolonged length of stay risk prediction leveraging historical electronic patient records
study_claim: The published metrics summarize the precision–recall curve.
observation: The code computes AUROC using binary predictions and calls it AUPRC. The expression equals balanced accuracy.
consequence: The affected figures measure balanced accuracy and leave the area under the precision–recall curve unknown.

title: Tangential Wasserstein Projections
study_claim: The barycentric projection implements a conditional expectation for the discrete distributions considered.
observation: baryc_proj normalizes rows separately without merging identical observations, returning different values for the same atom despite E[Y∣X=x].
consequence: Repeated input values can receive incompatible predictions.

title: ODE-based learning on manifold and its expressive power
journal: Advances in Continuous and Discrete Models 2026, article 25
study_claim: The proposed local fields realize any invertible differentiable transformation of the space.
observation: Theorem 3 restricts the fields to a fixed tubular neighborhood, forcing homotopy to the identity on the manifold.
consequence: Transformations in another homotopy class fall outside the claimed representation.

title: Personalized decision making for coronary artery disease treatment using offline reinforcement learning
study_claim: The algorithm learns a clinical policy from rewards observed for each transition.
observation: The code passes summed transition rewards to the algorithm. It normalizes the probabilities but never divides the rewards by their frequencies.
consequence: A historically frequent transition can be favored even when its average benefit is smaller.

title: Construct prognostic models of multiple myeloma with pathway information incorporated
study_claim: A test on resampled predictions supports significant differences between models.
observation: test.fun applies a signed-rank test to 1,000 paired bootstrap statistics. This compares their conditional distributions rather than establishing population uncertainty about superiority.
consequence: The comparison cannot show that the advantage persists in new patients.

title: Biological Sequence Kernels with Guaranteed Flexibility
study_claim: The kernel can approximate every continuous function vanishing at infinity under the stated injection.
observation: Proposition 27 claims C0-universality for every injective F. Accumulation in its image imposes continuity incompatible with approximating certain finitely supported functions.
consequence: Some finitely supported functions fall outside the promised approximation.

title: Real-time prediction of intensive care unit patient acuity and therapy requirements using state-space modelling
study_claim: The model uses the same comorbidity encoding across the two cohorts.
observation: eICU converts weighted Charlson indicators to binary values. MIMIC keeps weights 2, 3 and 6 in the same columns. The architecture and scaler are shared.
consequence: A verified patch aligns the encodings. Its effect on clinical accuracy remains unmeasured.

title: Jackpot: Approximating Uncertainty Domains with Adversarial Manifolds
study_claim: The stated differentiability conditions ensure a unique nearby local minimum.
observation: Theorems 5 and 21 assert uniqueness under C1 regularity alone, which allows bifurcations arbitrarily near the reference point.
consequence: Multiple nearby solutions can coexist under the stated conditions.

title: Jackpot 2.0 : variété d’incertitude pour les problèmes inverses
journal: 30e Colloque GRETSI sur le traitement du signal et des images, Strasbourg, pp.765–768, 2025
study_claim: A constant combination of epidemic parameters preserves the trajectory of infections.
observation: Proposition 4.1 holds βS0−γ constant and claims to preserve I(t). This fixes only the initial slope. Later values can change.
consequence: Measurements after the start can distinguish parameters that have the same initial slope.

title: Riemannian Bilevel Optimization
study_claim: The estimator's variability stays bounded by constants independent of Q.
observation: Under all the stated stochastic assumptions, the variance bounded in Lemma 21 can grow exponentially with Q.
consequence: The uncertainty can grow much faster as Q increases than the bound allows.

title: Multimodal CustOmics: A unified and interpretable multi-task deep learning framework for multimodal integrative data analysis in oncology
study_claim: The survival component learns differences in patients' prognosis.
observation: Softmax is applied to a single output, returning a constant risk of one and an exactly zero survival gradient.
consequence: The published branch assigns everyone the same risk and cannot learn risk differences.

title: Machine learning-based forecasting of daily acute ischemic stroke admissions using weather data
study_claim: Daily weather helps forecast admissions before they occur.
observation: Weather station selection and weights use locations of patients admitted on the target day. Those future locations are unavailable at forecast time.
consequence: A prospective forecast needs testing with weather inputs available before the admissions.

title: Self-improving generative foundation model for synthetic medical image generation and clinical applications
study_claim: Inception Score compares class distributions in generated medical images.
observation: calculate_IS omits class-probability weights and averages over both images and classes, forcing the result to be at most one.
consequence: The code's figures cannot be interpreted or compared as standard Inception Scores.

title: Mean-Field Variational Inference via Wasserstein Gradient Flow
study_claim: The entropy objective favors the desired transported distribution under general transformations.
observation: Equation 40 applies an identity for injective maps to arbitrary maps. Extra preimages can increase the objective without changing the transported distribution.
consequence: The objective can reward the transformation's multiplicity rather than a better distribution.

title: CLEO closed loop framework for synthesizing medical privacy preserving tabular data
study_claim: Synthetic data retain predictive utility on held-out patients.
observation: downstream.py splits train.csv after the generator has already received that entire file, including its target values. Classifiers train on its synthetic samples.
consequence: Evaluation on these patients cannot establish utility for genuinely unseen patients.

title: Explainable AI unravels sepsis heterogeneity via coagulation-inflammation profiles for prognosis and stratification
study_claim: Blood profiles distinguish sepsis subtypes in the evaluation set.
observation: The local pipeline splits an already oversampled file. Evaluation contains augmented profiles and profiles shared with training. We reproduced the exported splits.
consequence: An independent evaluation is needed to quantify subtype discrimination in new blood profiles.

title: Ten Machine Learning Models for Predicting Preoperative and Postoperative Coagulopathy in Patients With Trauma: Multicenter Cohort Study
study_claim: The held-out set evaluates coagulopathy prediction in new patients.
observation: After the split, Lasso selects features using the entire internal cohort and its labels, including the held-out outcomes.
consequence: Performance needs checking in patients completely excluded from feature selection.

title: Variance-Aware Estimation of Kernel Mean Embedding
study_claim: The intervals account for uncertainty in the kernel mean.
observation: The unnormalized variance term is multiplied by 2Δk a second time. This breaks kernel homogeneity and can narrow the intervals.
consequence: Changing the scale can leave the intervals with less coverage than intended.

title: Development and prospective validation of postoperative pain prediction from preoperative EHR data using attention-based set embeddings
study_claim: The statistical comparison identifies population differences in postoperative pain prediction.
observation: The code applies a Wilcoxon rank-sum test to 2,000 bootstrap RMSEs per method. This compares conditional bootstrap distributions, not population-level differences.
consequence: The test cannot establish the advantage in new patients.

title: Towards Unified Native Spaces in Kernel Methods
study_claim: Sobolev equivalence characterizes which functions the kernel can approximate.
observation: The proof controls high frequencies but ignores a spectral zero at the origin. For positive k this can preclude global Sobolev equivalence.
consequence: Low-frequency behavior can exclude functions the claimed equivalence includes.

title: Detection of breast cancer using machine learning on time-series diffuse optical transillumination data
study_claim: Bilateral optical data classify breast cancer in an independent evaluation.
observation: The classifier selects variables using diagnoses from the final test set. Separate column selection also changes how test features match training features.
consequence: Independent, consistently aligned evaluation is needed before interpreting the reported diagnostic accuracy.

title: Screening for extranodal extension in HPV-associated oropharyngeal carcinoma: evaluation of a CT-based deep learning algorithm in patient data from a multicentre, randomised de-escalation trial
study_claim: The evaluation measures calibration of extranodal extension risk.
observation: ECE receives complements of predicted probabilities instead of clinical outcomes. The manual plots swap observed and predicted axes without changing their labels.
consequence: Those curves cannot establish whether predicted risks match clinical outcomes.

title: CAP: Conformalized Abstention Policies for Context-Adaptive Risk Management for LLMs and VLMs
study_claim: The abstention rule controls risk when thresholds adapt to each input.
observation: The proof applies a marginal guarantee to an input-dependent threshold. This requires conditional coverage missing from general split conformal prediction. Equations 6–7 repeat the claim.
consequence: Selecting responses by input can exceed the risk guaranteed at a fixed threshold.

title: Landing with the Score: Riemannian Optimization through Denoising
study_claim: Scaled posterior covariance recovers the tangent projection of the support.
observation: Full support and a C3 density do not ensure strictly positive density. At a quadratic zero, the limit is three times the tangent projection.
consequence: A vanishing density can change the geometric estimator's scale.

title: Neural Hamilton–Jacobi Characteristic Flows for Optimal Transport
study_claim: Small loss guarantees close maps under the stated covariance bounds.
observation: Assumption 5.3 bounds covariance from above only. Theorem 5.4 omits dependence on a lower bound. Near-concentrated distributions can yield arbitrarily small loss.
consequence: Very different maps can fit concentrated data equally well.

title: Prediction of American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status Classification from preoperative clinical text narratives using natural language processing
study_claim: Statistical comparisons support the superiority of certain anesthesia classification models.
observation: The analysis treats bootstrap statistics as independent observations when comparing models.
consequence: The reported tests do not establish which model classifies new patients best.

title: Prognosis Individualized: Survival predictions for WHO grade II and III gliomas with a machine learning-based web application
study_claim: The published metrics and intervals quantify prognostic accuracy for gliomas.
observation: Sensitivity and specificity intervals use the total sample size instead of class-specific counts. All 16 intervals in Table 2 reproduce that choice.
consequence: The uncertainty is larger, and some accuracy figures require recalculation.

title: A multimodal knowledge-enhanced whole-slide pathology foundation model
study_claim: The final test measures generalization of a multimodal pathology prognosis model.
observation: The program combines validation and test data in val_loader and selects the highest C-index on that combined set during training.
consequence: The patients in the final test already contributed to model selection.

title: Functional optimal transport: regularized map estimation and domain adaptation for functional data
study_claim: Regularization gives a unique optimal operator for functional domain adaptation.
observation: Quadratic regularization does not make Wasserstein fitting convex for arbitrary operators; symmetric distributions can admit multiple solutions.
consequence: Different maps can fit two domains equally well despite the quadratic penalty.

title: Empirical comparison of routinely collected electronic health record data for head and neck cancer-specific survival in machine-learnt prognostic models
study_claim: The models predict clinical outcomes in an independent sample.
observation: SMOTE uses all patients before the train–test split, allowing original future test patients to influence the resampled data.
consequence: Testing on real patients without interpolated observations could change the differences between models.

title: Improved prediction of postoperative pediatric cerebellar mutism syndrome using an artificial neural network
study_claim: Tests across data splits support improved prediction of postoperative cerebellar mutism.
observation: Wilcoxon treats 100 repeated fold results as independent differences although the same 204 subjects recur.
consequence: The statistical advantage can disappear when each child counts once.

title: Boundary constrained Gaussian processes for robust physics-informed machine learning of linear partial differential equations
study_claim: The Gaussian construction satisfies the wave problem's boundary conditions.
observation: Wave-IBVP-1 uses an unnormalized distance function where normalization is required to cancel derivatives.
consequence: Sampled solutions can violate the derivative condition at both endpoints.

title: Spherical Rotation Dimension Reduction with Geometric Loss Functions
study_claim: Geometric reduction converges to the minimum under the proposed bounds.
observation: Theorem 1 bounds data, radius and matrix but allows suboptimal stationary points.
consequence: Sphere fitting can stop at a stationary solution that is not the minimum.

title: Medical multimodal multitask foundation model for lung cancer screening
study_claim: The model estimates cumulative lung cancer risk over follow-up.
observation: Hazard_Layer declares ReLU but never applies it. Unrestricted increments are summed before the sigmoid and can be negative.
consequence: Predicted cumulative risk can decrease, contradicting that output's probability interpretation.

title: Infinite-Dimensional Diffusion Models
study_claim: The bound controls diffusion error even as numerical error vanishes.
observation: A permitted Gaussian initialization can produce more Wasserstein error than Theorem 14 allows.
consequence: Distributional error can exceed the stated guarantee even with negligible numerical error.

title: Advancing precision prognostication in neuro-oncology: Machine learning models for data-driven personalized survival predictions in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma
study_claim: The intervals quantify uncertainty in sensitivity and specificity for neuro-oncology.
observation: Both intervals use total test size, although each metric uses only patients in its corresponding class.
consequence: Counting only the relevant class increases each metric's margin of error.

title: Machine Learning–Driven Prognostication in Traumatic Subdural Hematoma: Development of a Predictive Web Application
study_claim: The balanced accuracy for subdural hematoma prognosis is 0.813 with a narrow interval.
observation: The interval treats balanced accuracy as a single binomial proportion rather than an average of class-specific proportions.
consequence: Compatible confusion matrices give a margin of error about twice as large.

title: Machine learning models on a web application to predict short-term postoperative outcomes following anterior cervical discectomy and fusion
study_claim: The postoperative tool has balanced accuracy 0.674 with the published interval.
observation: The interval treats balanced accuracy as a single binomial proportion rather than an average of class-specific proportions.
consequence: Under the published definitions, the compatible margin exceeds 2.4 times the stated margin.

title: Vector-Valued Gaussian Processes for Approximating Divergence- or Rotation-free Vector Fields
study_claim: The proposed space contains all divergence-free fields on the three-dimensional domain.
observation: Simple connectivity in three dimensions does not ensure a global solenoidal extension. Theorem 22 relies on that identification.
consequence: The Gaussian representation can exclude fields permitted by the domain's geometry.

title: Sliced Wasserstein Regression
study_claim: Fourier approximation converges uniformly for functions smooth on their support.
observation: The proof confuses smoothness on the support with smoothness of the zero extension. Fourier truncation can leave boundary error.
consequence: Increasing the number of frequencies need not remove the error at the edge.

title: AI-powered spatial cell phenomics enhances risk stratification in non-small cell lung cancer
study_claim: Cellular phenomics improves risk stratification in lung cancer.
observation: Figure 6A applies Mann–Whitney to 10,000 bootstrap replicates as if those replicates replaced patients as independent units.
consequence: A paired comparison of the published adenocarcinoma risks does not detect that advantage.

title: Training a high-performance retinal foundation model with half-the-data and 400 times less compute
study_claim: The new retinal model outperforms comparators according to AUC tests.
observation: The procedure applies Wilcoxon to 100 bootstrap AUCs from the same test set, using resamples in place of independent patients.
consequence: A claim of superiority needs a comparison that measures variability between patients.

title: Functional data analysis for multivariate distributions through Wasserstein slicing
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38, Main Conference, NeurIPS 2025
study_claim: The representation of functional distributions stays bounded under the stated positivity assumption.
observation: A positive joint density on its support does not guarantee a positive lower bound for its marginals.
consequence: The representation can grow without bound as the support narrows.

title: Estimating diagnostic uncertainty in artificial intelligence assisted pathology using conformal prediction
study_claim: A smoothed p-value quantifies diagnostic uncertainty when scores tie.
observation: The smoothed p-value omits the test observation's own contribution to ties. The smallest test observation receives zero.
consequence: A tied result can appear to provide stronger evidence than it does.

title: Fréchet Geodesic Boosting
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38, Main Conference, NeurIPS 2025
study_claim: The ensemble uniformly controls population prediction risk.
observation: The proof derives a uniform law from pointwise convergence and equicontinuity, without controlling the complexity of the full span.
consequence: An ensemble can fit the sample perfectly while retaining population error.

title: Decoding cancer circulating transcriptomic signatures with language models
study_claim: Changes in AUC across variants measure the contribution of transcriptomic components.
observation: Table 1 AUCs reconstruct using different evaluation populations and labels.
consequence: The AUC differences may reflect which patients and labels entered each comparison.

title: Transformers from Diffusion: A Unified Framework for Neural Message Passing
study_claim: The stated update equation produces the published numerical examples.
observation: Equation 6 preserves every constant signal for any S. The reported example updates conflict with that property.
consequence: Reproducing the examples requires reconciling the equation and numerical updates.

title: GlioSurv: interpretable transformer for multimodal, individualized survival prediction in diffuse glioma
study_claim: The model checkpoint preserves the best validation concordance during training.
observation: GlioSurvTrainer.run sets val_max_c_index unconditionally and overwrites best_c_index.pth.tar each epoch.
consequence: The stored checkpoint can correspond to the final epoch rather than the best validation epoch.

title: Synaptic loss pattern is constrained by brain connectome and modulated by phosphorylated tau in Alzheimer’s disease
study_claim: The bootstrap comparison supports the reported association in Figure 2m.
observation: A paired t-test treats 1,000 bootstrap coefficients as independent observations, dividing sampling uncertainty by √1,000 again.
consequence: Assessing precision requires uncertainty across independent observations, not the number of resamples.

title: A generalizable pathology foundation model using a unified knowledge distillation pretraining framework
study_claim: Resampled differences support advantages for a generalist pathology model.
observation: Wilcoxon compares 1,000 metrics resampled from the same dataset. This tests conditional distributions rather than equal population performance.
consequence: Reported significance can increase with more resamples even if the patient data stay fixed.

title: Deep learning signature based on multiphase enhanced CT for bladder cancer recurrence prediction: a multi-center study
study_claim: A bladder recurrence model retains calibration in an external cohort.
observation: The evaluation replaces trained probabilities for four models with probabilities refitted to external outcomes. Bootstrap validation then assesses those refits internally.
consequence: The procedure cannot establish external calibration of the original probabilities.

title: Conformal Risk Training: End-to-End Optimization of Conformal Risk Control
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38, NeurIPS 2025 Main Conference
study_claim: The fallback mechanism controls risk after selection of the final option.
observation: Marginal feasibility of each fallback does not preserve control after choosing one using calibration data.
consequence: The selected fallback can exceed the risk limit even when each option is marginally valid.

title: A Machine Learning-Based Online Prediction Tool for Predicting Short-Term Postoperative Outcomes Following Spinal Tumor Resections
study_claim: The table reports precision and sensitivity separately for postoperative predictors.
observation: The metric arguments are reversed. All twelve rows of Table 1 reproduce sensitivity labeled precision and precision labeled sensitivity.
consequence: The affected entries answer different clinical questions and need relabeling.

title: Optimal Functional Bilinear Regression with Two-dimensional Functional Covariates via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space
study_claim: The estimator converges uniformly over every function in the specified space.
observation: Theorem 2 takes a supremum over all of H(K) without a norm bound. In an allowed Gaussian submodel the supremum of the error probability stays at one rather than tending to zero.
consequence: Without a norm restriction, large errors can persist at any sample size.

title: ConfHit: Conformal Generative Design with Oracle-Free Guarantees
journal: International Conference on Learning Representations 2026, Main Conference
study_claim: The procedure certifies properties of generated candidates without consulting the oracle.
observation: Candidates are reordered internally, but their properties are evaluated in the original order.
consequence: A certificate can be attached to a different candidate from the one evaluated.

title: Conformal Linguistic Calibration: Trading-off between Factuality and Specificity
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38, NeurIPS 2025 Main Conference
study_claim: The selected thresholds control the trade-off between factual accuracy and linguistic specificity.
observation: Each threshold is tested at the full level, with no familywise adjustment or sequential testing.
consequence: Choosing among multiple thresholds can push the joint risk above its intended level.

title: LaplacianFormer:Rethinking Linear Attention with Laplacian Kernel
study_claim: An approximate inverse provides efficient Laplacian kernel attention.
observation: Algorithm 1 uses a generally non-symmetric cross-kernel W. Its CUDA inverse initializes using W+.01I without transposing it. An allowed matrix gives a residual spectral radius above one.
consequence: The numerical iteration can diverge on a matrix permitted by the algorithm.

title: Bayesian Sparse Gaussian Mixture Model for Clustering in High Dimensions
study_claim: The model guarantees a bounded number of errors when separating Gaussian groups.
observation: Theorem 8 permits constant mean separation but bounds the number of incorrect labels. Two allowed Gaussians have positive Bayes error even when their parameters are known.
consequence: For overlapping groups, the expected number of errors can grow with sample size.

title: Deep mutational scanning of the human insulin receptor ectodomain to inform precision therapy for insulin resistance
study_claim: The assay identifies variants whose effects differ from the null distribution.
observation: The bootstrap treats copies of a single mean as independent barcodes. A mean can recur five times, narrowing the null reference for a single-barcode variant.
consequence: Some single-barcode variants can appear better supported than the evidence warrants.

title: Conformal Tail Risk Control for Large Language Model Alignment
journal: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR267:8955–8978
study_claim: The VaR variant gives statistical tail-risk control during alignment.
observation: The VaR calculation divides uncertainty by the sample-size scale twice.
consequence: Tail uncertainty can be underestimated, admitting configurations with excessive risk.

title: Flexynesis: A deep learning toolkit for bulk multi-omics data integration for precision oncology and beyond
study_claim: The tests distinguish population performance of models that combine multiple omics data types.
observation: Paired t-tests on 100 bootstrap results divide an existing estimate of test-set uncertainty by √100 again. This measures Monte Carlo precision.
consequence: Adding resamples can create apparent significance with exactly the same patients and predictions.

title: CLADES: a hybrid NeuralODE-Gillespie approach for unveiling clonal cell fate and differentiation dynamics
study_claim: Comparative tests support differences between models of cell fate and differentiation.
observation: The t and Mann–Whitney tests treat bootstrap estimates as independent observations. Their significance then depends on the number of computational replicates.
consequence: The statistical conclusion can change with more resamples and no new experiments.

title: Germline functional variants contribute to somatic mutation and outcomes in neuroblastoma
study_claim: The test cohort externally validates five neuroblastoma prognosis models.
observation: The testing block refits all five Cox models using test outcomes and extracts apparent concordance via validate(fit)[1,1]. The training coefficients are never evaluated there.
consequence: Test concordance describes the refitted models. External validation of the original models remains outstanding.

title: The evolutionary drivers and correlates of viral host jumps
study_claim: Evolutionary associations with host jumps persist after dominant groups are excluded.
observation: The robustness test uses 1,000 resamples as the t-test sample size. Its denominator measures Monte Carlo precision rather than variation between events.
consequence: Assessing the robustness of this comparison requires uncertainty across independent events.

title: CGRiC: Compositional Risk Certification for Structured LLM Outputs
journal: Proceedings of the43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR306:112472–112496
study_claim: The certificate combines component risks to control the model's structured outputs.
observation: Theorem 3 combines conditional independence with marginal bounds as though the components were unconditionally independent.
consequence: Marginal dependence can make the combined risk exceed the bound.

title: Conformal Risk-Averse Decision Making with Action Conditional Guarantee
journal: Proceedings of the43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR306:167248–167276
study_claim: The calibrator guarantees risk control for every selected action.
observation: Calibration can stop at a solution that violates the action-conditional guarantee.
consequence: An action can exceed its risk target even after the calibrator stops updating.

title: Contact Wasserstein Geodesics for Non-Conservative Schrödinger Bridges
study_claim: Two non-conservative transport problems yield the same optimal paths.
observation: With identical endpoints, a positive Riemannian energy is minimized by constant density. The published SB problem allows a smooth excursion at strictly lower cost.
consequence: The two problems can predict different paths even with identical starting and ending densities.

title: A map of the rubisco biochemical landscape
study_claim: The fitted curve describes the relationship between carbon dioxide and biochemical performance.
observation: The reproduction pipeline swaps concentration and enrichment in the Michaelis–Menten fit. Bootstrap fitting uses CO₂ as the response, reversing the documented regression direction.
consequence: The reproduced kinetic parameters correspond to a different regression.

title: Generalized Resubstitution for Regression Error Estimation
study_claim: Gaussian smoothing with fixed covariance consistently estimates regression risk.
observation: Proposition 11 assumes finite VC dimension and fixed covariance. A bounded example converges to the smoothed risk rather than the original risk.
consequence: Even with more observations, the estimator can converge to the risk of a different model.

title: Stochastic Differential Equations models for Least-Squares Stochastic Gradient Descent
study_claim: Under the stated noisy conditions the distribution develops infinite moments.
observation: Proposition 10 predicts infinite moments for n≥2d. An allowed normalized full-rank design removes effective multiplicative noise, yielding a Gaussian stationary distribution.
consequence: A permitted design can have finite moments instead of the predicted heavy tails.

title: Clinical usability of an explainable AI decision support tool and evaluation of multimodal models in NSCLC
study_claim: The survival objective correctly handles patients with tied follow-up times.
observation: The public Cox objective omits risk-set members at ties. Reordering simultaneous events and censoring changes the loss and gradients.
consequence: Simply reordering patients with identical follow-up can change training.

title: AutoPrognosis 2.0: Democratizing diagnostic and prognostic modeling in healthcare with automated machine learning
study_claim: The ensemble combines survival distributions into valid probabilities over time.
observation: Mixing cumulative increments with time-varying weights does not preserve probability mass.
consequence: The combined probabilities can lose mass as the weights change between intervals.

title: Machine learning models for prediction of lymph node metastasis in patients with gastric cancer: a Chinese single-centre study with external validation in an Asian American population
study_claim: The models are ranked by their ability to predict lymph-node metastasis.
observation: The bootstrap accumulator persists across metrics. Precision, F1, sensitivity and specificity mix earlier distributions. The reproduction matches 120 reported values.
consequence: Resetting the accumulator reverses the F1 ranking in the affected comparison.

title: Simulation-based Calibration of Uncertainty Intervals under Approximate Bayesian Estimation
study_claim: The adjustment calibrates widths of intervals from approximate Bayesian inference.
observation: The method uses a standard deviation as a multiplicative factor for a variance.
consequence: The adjusted intervals can have a different scale and coverage from those intended.

title: CalPro: Prior-Aware Evidential Conformal Prediction with Structure-Aware Sensitivity Bounds for Protein Structures
study_claim: Distributional distance linearly bounds changes in thresholded conformal predictions.
observation: Thresholded probability changes are not bounded linearly by W1 in general.
consequence: Small shifts around the threshold can change predictions far more than the bound permits.

title: Unsupervised Feature Selection via Nonnegative Orthogonal Constrained Regularized Minimization
study_claim: The algorithm converges to feasible solutions for constrained feature selection.
observation: Theorems 10 and 11 claim all accumulation points are feasible. A permitted sequence has zero interior criticality, clipped constant multipliers and a feasibility residual tending to 1/4.
consequence: An admissible sequence can retain a constraint violation of 0.25 in the limit.

title: Inference-Time Conformal Reasoning with Valid Factuality Control for Large Language Models
study_claim: Calibration controls the risk of missing a correct answer during reasoning.
observation: The no-miss branch calibrates and evaluates the last error-free prefix, which is a different target.
consequence: The computed guarantee applies to that last correct prefix rather than the stated objective.

title: N-Orbit: towards a universal model and metric for comparing tissue microenvironments
study_claim: A permutation test detects enriched motifs in tissue microenvironments.
observation: The enrichment test ignores permutations with zero occurrences of a motif. A highly enriched motif can receive p=1.
consequence: The test can miss a motif frequent in tissue but absent from many permutations.

title: A consensus immune dysregulation framework for sepsis and critical illnesses
study_claim: The figure estimates a treatment difference among the patients shown.
observation: Figure 6e displays 117 patients but includes 59 others in its tests. Patients lacking a second drug are automatically placed in the comparison group.
consequence: The reported significance depends on patients outside the figure and does not describe the plotted counts alone.

title: CiteGuard: Conformal False-Discovery Control for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
study_claim: The false citation proportion concentrates exponentially around its mean.
observation: Proposition D.1 claims exponential concentration of FDP around FDR without controlling random denominators.
consequence: An individual response can have more false citations than the concentration claim predicts.

title: A data-driven latent variable approach to validating the research domain criteria framework
study_claim: Fit tests establish superior and generalizable performance for certain neurobiological models.
observation: ANOVA and Mann–Whitney compare distributions from 5,000 bootstrap fits. The procedure fails under a symmetric CFA null model.
consequence: It can report significant differences even between equivalent population models.

title: Test-time Verification via Optimal Transport: Coverage, ROC, & Sub-optimality
study_claim: The rule identifies when unlimited batch size preserves the intended coverage.
observation: The unlimited-batch test compares chi-square with beta, although its derivation requires beta−1.
consequence: The procedure can authorize unlimited batches for parameter values outside the derived condition.

title: Exploring Novel Uncertainty Quantification through Forward Intensity Function Modeling
study_claim: Event and censoring estimation errors have zero cross-covariance.
observation: Theorem 1 sets their cross-covariances to zero. An admissible Markov process gives four nonzero covariances and also contradicts Lemma 10.
consequence: Ignoring this dependence can change uncertainty estimates in follow-up models.

title: Generative AI-powered multimodal physiological sensors for personalized edge health monitoring
study_claim: Five data splits support an improvement with two-sided p<0.001.
observation: With five pairs the smallest exact two-sided Wilcoxon p-value is 0.0625.
consequence: That exact test cannot establish significance at 5% with five pairs.

title: Recent, but not long-term, priors induce behavioral oscillations in peri-saccadic vision
study_claim: The permutation test evaluates behavioral oscillations while preserving within-participant comparisons.
observation: The Methods permute within participants. The code mixes trials across participants. These null distributions differ with heterogeneous intercepts and timing.
consequence: Individual differences can change the threshold used to attribute oscillations to expectations.

title: Underdamped Langevin MCMC with third order convergence
study_claim: Sampling error is controlled by initial discrepancy in positions.
observation: The bound uses only the initial marginal W2 discrepancy in position, omitting initial dependence between position and velocity.
consequence: Initial position–velocity dependence can also determine later sampling error.

title: Computable longitudinal patient journeys from structured and unstructured EHR data
study_claim: The bands estimate uncertainty in clinical changes from baseline.
observation: The analysis subtracts an estimated baseline prediction from means and limits while retaining level variance. It omits baseline estimation uncertainty and covariance.
consequence: Individual-change precision also requires the uncertainty of the estimated reference.

title: Histological aging signatures for monitoring tissue-specific aging and disease
study_claim: Validation metrics describe how well histological aging signatures generalize.
observation: The helper labels training correlations and explained variance as validation metrics. The published table reproduces 80 copied values.
consequence: Those 80 figures describe training fit. They require checking against held-out tissues.

title: A full life cycle biological clock based on routine clinical data and its impact in health and diseases
study_claim: The biological clock estimates age using the clinical history available at each visit.
observation: Three BertEncoder modules without causal masks reintroduce later visits after the causal GPT2 stage.
consequence: Retrospective estimates can use visits unavailable at prediction time.

title: Stereographic Spherical Sliced Wasserstein Distances
study_claim: The stereographic distance is well-defined under the published spherical moment condition.
observation: Theorem 3.2 requires transformed moments: finite spherical moments do not ensure finite stereographic Wasserstein distance.
consequence: We withdrew the antipodal example. With infinite support, projection can still yield an infinite distance.
